thread:
ashley: FYI we just got a customer escalation — p99 latency for /v1/generate in eu-west jumped from ~120ms to ~1.2s starting ~08:00 UTC. They included traces showing long TLS handshake. Kicking this to eng-sre.

maria: assigning. I'm oncall. Which POPs are affected? Any SIGs in metrics?

ashley: Seems concentrated on eu-west-1 region (customers hitting eu-west edge). Support provided sample request_ids: req_az1, req_az2. Grafana shows p95 stable but p99 spike ~08:02-08:15. No increase in error rate.

deploy-bot: alert: latency_spike_detected /v1/generate p99 eu-west (08:03 UTC). CPU/GPU util normal, connection churn low.

raj: pinged the edge routing team — initial thought: geo-handoff/DNS-anycast wobble or cross-AZ TLS handshake retry causing tail latency. Any traceroutes or mtr from customer?

ashley: customer pasted a small set:
```
traceroute to edge.redwood.example (52.16.8.5), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.0.1  0.4 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  12.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.2  20.5 ms
 4  203.0.113.10  58.3 ms
 5  52.16.8.5  59.1 ms
```
But they also ran openssl s_client timing: handshake sometimes 900-1100 ms.
```
openssl s_time -connect edge.redwood.example:443 -new -time 1
# avg handshake 0.95s
```

maria: interesting — path is short but handshake is long. That suggests server-side TLS delay (maybe session resumption issues) or intermediate TCP/TLS proxy introducing extra RTTs. Are we seeing increased TLS retry logs on the edge? Jordan, can you pull TLS accept histograms for the eu-west POPs?

jordan: I'm on it. Fetching from edge-pop-metrics/eu-west/*

jordan: quick grep shows spike in tls_handshake_time_bucket > 500ms at 08:02 on pop-eu-west-3. Also seeing increased "ssl renegotiate" entries in logs around same time.

raj: Could be a particular instance/host in the pop degraded or a new kernel update that affected BoringSSL behavior. Any recent deploys to pop-eu-west-3?

maria: Looking at deploy history — no app deploys 07:30-09:00, but there was an infra patch build rolled to eu-west-3 at 07:58 (kernel backports for networking). Patch id: infra-2026-07. Rolled to 3/5 hosts in that pop, flagged as completed.

ashley: support: customer confirms issue started ~08:00 which maps. They are impacted heavily.

raj: OK that narrows it down. If kernel backport changed TLS buffer handling or cong control, it could add handshake time for cold sessions. Mitigation path: 1) rollback infra patch on affected hosts 2) route traffic away from pop-eu-west-3 (failover) 3) enable session-resumption reminders (longer session tickets) as short-term.

maria: I'd prefer immediate traffic routing change so we stop serving traffic from that pop while we troubleshoot. Can we shift weight off pop-eu-west-3 to eu-west-1/2?

jordan: We can change the LB weight for pop-eu-west-3 to 0 in router-config, but need to ensure capacity in other POPs. Current capacity headroom is ~18%. I'll start a Canary reroute at 10% -> 0 to observe.

raj: Meanwhile I'll open SSH to the patched hosts and gather strace/sslsniff logs. If handshake stalls at accept() or after, that'll tell us if kernel/root cause.

maria: Action plan then: 1) jordan: gradually drain pop-eu-west-3 (start now) 2) raj: collect tls accept traces + check dmesg/kernel logs for backports 3) ashley/support: notify customer we've enacted failover and are investigating 4) if quick root-cause on patch, roll back hosts.

jordan: Starting weight change now. Running:
```
routerctl set-weight --pop pop-eu-west-3 5
# wait 30s
routerctl set-weight --pop pop-eu-west-3 0
```

jordan: Done. Monitoring.

maria: Observing graph — p99 for /v1/generate in eu-west dropping from ~1.2s -> ~180ms within 2 minutes. Nice.

ashley: Customer updated: latency back to normal for new requests. They asked for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.

raj: On hosts now. I can reproduce handshake tail by running repeated openssl s_client. Getting occasional 1s handshakes on the patched kernel. dmesg shows new TLS helper warnings around the same timestamp and a WARN about skb cloning in kTLS path.

maria: That aligns — kernel backport (infra-2026-07) introduced an optimization change that interacts poorly with our userland TLS stack for short-lived sessions. We should roll back the patch on the remaining two hosts in pop-eu-west-3.

raj: Rolling back now on host-a and host-b. Commands:
```
apt-get remove --allow-downgrades infra-kernel-backport-2026-07 -y
reboot
```
Rebooting host-a (host-b next).

deploy-bot: rollout: infra-rollback initiated for pop-eu-west-3 hosts.

jordan: After rollback hosts rejoin. p99 stable. No errors in TLS logs.

maria: Summarizing for customer and postmortem: root cause = infra kernel backport infra-2026-07 introduced kTLS/skb handling change causing intermittent TLS handshake tail latency on patched hosts. Impact = ~08:00-08:12 UTC; affected pop = pop-eu-west-3; user-facing p99 spike up to ~1.2s. Mitigations = drained pop and rolled back patch on patched hosts; longer-term fix = validate kernel backport in staging with kTLS-enabled traffic, add canary checks for TLS handshake latency during infra rollouts, and add automated pop-weight rollback if p99 exceeds threshold for 5m.

ashley: I'll send customer an update and open a support case note.

maria: Opening incident ticket for tracking and postmortem. Adding owners: raj (engineer), jordan (routing), ashley (customer comms).

srebot: incident created: INC-2026-0843.

raj: Follow-ups for postmortem: reproduce in staging with the exact kernel backport, file bug upstream with kernel maintainers, add a preflight test that exercises short-lived TLS sessions at scale.

maria: Great. Closing slack thread once incident ticket has summary attached. Thanks all :thumbsup:

ashley: Customer replied: "appreciate the quick response and rollback — will monitor from our side." :heart:

raj: leaving a note in infra-change log: revert infra-2026-07 for eu-west 2026-07-15 08:10 UTC.

maria: last message: we'll draft full RCA and circulate tomorrow. Good job team.
